title: Kernel Replay Seed Factory — deterministic kernel-choice recording and offline repro pipeline
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: Kernel selection currently uses a mix of heuristics, probes, and nondeterministic samplers for exploration. This makes offline debugging, long-term regression analysis, and safe offline autotuning difficult because we cannot deterministically reproduce a request's kernel choice.

Goal: Add a lightweight, deterministic 'seed factory' that records the RNG seeds and deterministic decision inputs used for kernel-choice (including architecture fingerprint, seq-length bucket, model variant hints, and probe outcomes). Expose a reproducible replay mode and an offline repro pipeline that can re-run decisions against historical telemetry to evaluate new kernel policies or surrogate models without impacting production traffic.

Why: Deterministic replay enables: 1) fair A/B comparisons of kernel policies using the exact same request stream; 2) targeted offline validation of fallback/quantized kernels for safety windows; 3) faster root-cause analysis for tail-latency regressions by reproducing exact execution paths.

Scope: record minimal deterministic inputs and an RNG seed per request decision point; provide a compact storage format with TTL; implement a server-side replay harness that can feed the recorded inputs into the kernel selector with pluggable policy implementations; add a feature-flagged shadow-execution mode that runs candidate kernels in a best-effort background worker to collect perf deltas (no production responses affected).
acceptance_criteria: Recorded seed + deterministic inputs can reproduce kernel choice end-to-end for >= 99% of sampled requests in the staging replay harness
Replay harness can process a 24h sampled request corpus (10k reqs) within 3 hours on CI runners with parallelism settings
Shadow-execution pipeline collects latency and memory delta for candidate kernels with <1% additional load on serving hosts (configurable budget)
Storage for recorded seeds stays under 5KB per request (compressed) and honors TTL policy configurable by route
Feature flag rollout with canary (10% traffic) and clear rollback path; no user-facing latency regressions during canary
Documentation added: design doc, ops runbook, and developer guide for how to run replays and interpret results
implementation_steps: Design compact recording schema (seed, request fingerprint, seq-len bucket, arch tag, probe summary, timestamp) - design doc in Confluence
Add recording hook in kernel-selector entrypoint; implement config to enable/disable recording per route
Implement TTL-backed storage in telemetry pipeline (Kafka topic + compacting consumer OR S3 batched export)
Build replay harness that can consume recorded blobs and re-run the selector deterministically; add unit/integration tests
Add shadow-execution worker that can be enabled per-cluster and runs candidate kernels off the critical path; collect perf deltas to metrics backend
Create feature flags and rollout plan (canary -> region -> global), implement safety limits for shadow worker resource usage
Add dashboards and alerts: replay success rate, shadow-exec errors, storage growth, reproduction mismatch rate
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (dev/staging): enable recording for selected routes, run replay harness on small corpus, validate deterministic behavior
Phase 2 (canary): enable recording + shadow-exec for 10% of traffic behind flag; monitor production metrics for 48h
Phase 3 (regional): expand canary to selected regions and run full-day replays nightly; validate storage and cost
Phase 4 (global): enable for all non-sensitive routes; start using replay corpus for offline autotuning experiments
Rollback criteria: reproduction mismatch >1%, >0.5% latency regression on canary, shadow-exec resource spike > configured budget
risks: Recording sensitive inputs could conflict with privacy/legal requirements — must sanitize any user payloads and honor PII rules
Storage growth could exceed budget if retention misconfigured — need TTL and sampling controls
Shadow execution could accidentally impact co-located workloads if resource limits are not enforced
Determinism assumptions may break with future selector changes (e.g., new nondeterministic kernels) — need compatibility guards
notes: Keep recorded payload minimal; prefer fingerprints over raw prompts. For routes with strict privacy requirements, support opt-out or sampled recording.
This system complements but does not replace existing live prober/autotune experiments; it's primarily for repro and offline validation of candidate policies.
We should coordinate with privacy/compliance and the console team to surface retention settings in the UI for enterprise tenants.
